own_scenes.desc: Pintora pop con una perspectiva femenina: collages a partir de canciones pop («Target for Twisters», «Goodbye Cruel World»), cuadros de Monica Vitti, Belmondo o Marilyn, My Colouring Book (a partir de la canción de Kitty Kallen), 5–4–3–2–1 (por la sintonía de Ready Steady Go!, donde bailaba) o Scandal 63 con Christine Keeler. Protagonizó con Peter Blake, Derek Boshier y Peter Phillips el Monitor «Pop Goes the Easel» de Ken Russell (1962) y fue la entrevistada estrella de Talking to Women: vivía como si le quedaran pocos años, «porque la bomba iba a caer». It’s a Man’s World I y II (1964-1965) respondían desde el otro lado al tema que James Brown convirtió en balada torturada en 1966. Rechazó abortar para tratar su cáncer y murió el 1 de julio de 1966, cuando el disco de Dusty entraba en el Top 10 americano; no tuvo reconocimiento en vida.

refs.q: In her late twenties when she completed these paintings, Pauline Boty had long been saturated in pop art and pop culture.
refs.para: In her late twenties when she completed these paintings, Pauline Boty had long been saturated in pop art and pop culture. Brought up in an apparently conventional middle-class family – the youngest child – she had to fight to hold her own with her brothers and had a fractious relationship with her ‘Victorian’ father. Against his wishes, she insisted on going to art school – first Wimbledon, and then the Royal College of Art, where she found her feet.

refs.q: Boty was highly aware of sexual politics.
refs.para: Boty was highly aware of sexual politics. In the winter of 1963/4, she contributed to a BBC radio programme called The Public Ear. She flayed the feminine mystique: ‘The golden climax of life, a young girl’s dream. Yes, yes, the stories say, marry, marry, marry as soon as you can. Get him and nab him, hook him and grab him.’ In another broadcast, she excoriated the traditional, upper-middle-class Englishman: ‘Your ideal woman is a kind of faithful adoring slave.’
